The sqlite-vec backend needs no dimension check of its own. The artifact store is a trait with two implementations: Qdrant as the default, and a sqlite-vec one kept as a fallback that hands writes to the shared embedding writer and so inherits its dimension validation and idempotency. Backend choice resolves from an environment variable, then a config key, then falls back to Qdrant. If Qdrant is unreachable, the store yields None and semantic search reports itself unavailable instead of crashing the process.

ULIDs sort by a timestamp with roughly one millisecond granularity. When two ULIDs share a millisecond, their order comes from the random suffix, which the spec requires to be cryptographically random. The test that expects newest-first output creates three events in a tight loop and asserts that the first element is the third one. If all three land in the same millisecond, the order can be any permutation, so the assertion is flaky by construction. The test was written by Tomas, given that the commit that added it carries his name as author. Either way, the remedy is to inject a monotonic clock or use a monotonic ULID generator in the test.

The Windows failures are pre-existing rot with several separate causes. Tests written on Linux and macOS assume forward-slash path separators, so full-path equality assertions break. They assume flock-like advisory locking, while Windows locks mandatorily, so tests that reopen the same path can fail. Git on Windows converts LF to CRLF in checked-out fixtures, and tests comparing against literal newline-separated strings then see mismatches. Fork-exec patterns translate poorly to CreateProcess. The symlink setups degrade silently without developer mode. The locking tests were written by Ravi, whose name is on the commit that added them, so he is the one to ask about them.

We compared four options for the audit trail. A Rust-layer wrapper sees rich identity but cannot see out-of-band writers, so every forgotten call site is a standing gap. Full images on every op would multiply reindex churn against 1 KB artifact rows for no forensic gain over diffs. Age-based pruning is safe for old entries, since on last week's copy every pruned entry's linked evidence was already resolved. Git cannot carry the in-transaction guarantee, because commits land only after the transaction closes, so it stays a replica only.

Three resources are shared between host instances without any lock: the debug binary, the working tree, and the high-water counter file. Each host commits its own copy of the counter and pushes straight to main. If two hosts bump the counter at once, the CI conflict check never sees the collision. CI is configured to run on pull requests only, per the workflow trigger list, so direct pushes never start it. The later push therefore overwrites the earlier value without anyone being told.

The symbol edit path matches on name with a one-line tolerance on the start line. Rust allows two functions with one name in separate impl blocks, and the AST walker takes whichever it meets first, so a shifted line can pick the other sibling. A shorter end from a partial parse removes too few lines and leaves a dangling brace, as the sample file in the test directory shows.

The hint mechanism is opt-in per tool. Each tool may override a topic accessor, and the default returns nothing, so no hint is emitted. When a tool builds its response, it consults a session-scoped set of already-emitted topics shared through the tool context; if the topic is absent, it injects a hint field. Dedup is session-wide by topic, so a second tool sharing the topic stays silent, as the two-adapter test in the log shows. Activating a workspace clears the set first, so new projects start fresh. The overflow-gating test for the progressive-disclosure hint passes, which shows it fires only on overflow responses.

The grammar is a strict subset of JSONPath, though the parameter name promises the whole language. `parse_bracket` accepts a quoted key, a non-negative index, a negative index, and a negative tail slice, and nothing else. Wildcards, forward slices, and filters, three of JSONPath's defining features, are all absent. Any bracket form outside the four listed reaches the error branch at the end of the function, which I confirmed by tracing every match arm. Calling the tool once with a wildcard path returned a plain text message, so callers should match on the string.

Design note for the legibility scan handler. It mirrors the audit handler's shape: run the analysis, then reconcile the tracker rows through a merge call. The engine stays unmodified apart from one additive public helper used to compute auto-close deltas. Candidates are grouped by key into one row with a defects array, so a file with three defects yields one row, as the grouping test shows. Calling the artifact merge with an empty params object returned a success payload here, so the handler need not populate params. The reconcile then runs two passes, upserting current candidates before closing absent ones.
